audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer rates the lane EVEN at 6/10 and hands Rumble levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items. Rumble is at 47.95% here, and the content layer's own level chart gives Ambessa everything from level 4 onward and never gives it back. The two layers describe different matchups.
audit.why: A sub-50 win rate with a stated 8.5/10 enemy carry threat and a content narrative that ends 'she wins the side lane' is not an even matchup. The content chart (Rumble, Rumble, Skill, Ambessa x4) matches the packet levelChart and matches the kit: Rumble's edge is the pre-Lacerate window and it closes permanently.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN to HARD, diffRating 6/10 to 7/10, and the Final Matchup Rating row aligned. The phases[].side values still disagree with the chart and could not be edited within the length band — flagged in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 1-2 spike claims Ambessa has no dash until 'her W dash', which is the reason given for Rumble's free early window. She has a dash from level 1: Drakehound's Step is her passive and fires off any ability cast.
audit.why: Riot's Drakehound's Step text: entering an attack or movement command while casting an ability makes her dash once the ability is cast, and empowers the next attack. So the free window at level 1 is real but narrower than described, and for the right reason — she has a step-in but no Lacerate to leave the cone with. The 4-5 spike is also mis-attributed to a 'W chain'; the repeatable dash there is Lacerate at 13/12/11/10/9 plus the passive.
audit.corrected: Both spikes restated with the correct abilities and Lacerate's real cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate problems. (a) The full layer names her defining ability 'Repeating Dashes' in fourteen places. No such ability exists. (b) The content layer calls her dash 'W' throughout — 'her W dash', 'her W chain', 'the first W hit'. W is Repudiation, which is not a dash at all. The dashes are Drakehound's Step (passive) and Lacerate (E). (c) The decisive interaction in the matchup is never mentioned: Repudiation braces, and if it blocks non-minion damage while bracing, the slam that follows deals increased damage. Walking a Flamespitter cone into a braced Repudiation actively loads her counterattack. Public Execution's targeting rule is also unstated — it blinks to the farthest enemy champion in the line she picks.
audit.why: The kit file is the authority on names and Ambessa's are Drakehound's Step, Cunning Sweep / Sundering Slam, Repudiation, Lacerate and Public Execution. Rumble's whole damage pattern is a sustained cone, which is the worst possible thing to feed a damage-scaling brace, so this is the single most important line in the matchup and it is absent. The Public Execution targeting rule changes where Rumble stands in a teamfight.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name removed and replaced with the real abilities; 'W dash' corrected to Lacerate / Drakehound's Step across the content layer; the Repudiation brace rule and Public Execution's farthest-target rule added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Ambessa cooldown number appears anywhere in either layer, despite 'track her cooldown' being the stated win condition.
audit.why: Lacerate is 13/12/11/10/9, Repudiation is 18/17/16/15/14, Cunning Sweep is 14/13/12/11/10 and Public Execution is 130/115/100. Repudiation at 18 seconds is the punishable one — it is her only defensive tool and the window after she spends it is the whole trade.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into the cooldown breakdown and the level 4-5 spike.

edits.before: At Level 1 you have the cleaner deal: walk into Flamespitter range and let her choose to take the damage or back off — she has no dash yet and no answer to sustained Q pressure. The moment she hits Level 2 and has her W, the dynamic shifts slightly; she can dash forward through the tip of your cone, take reduced Flamespitter ticks, and reposition around your slow. Your job in these first three levels is to bank small chip damage with Q, threaten the double Electro-Harpoon when she overextends, and never let her bait a full combo while your Heat is at 0 — an Overheat silence here is a free trade for her.
edits.after: At Level 1 you have the cleaner deal: walk into Flamespitter range and let her choose to take the damage or back off — Drakehound's Step gets her in, but nothing gets her out. Once Lacerate is up the dynamic shifts; she can dash through the tip of your cone, eat reduced ticks, and step around your slow. Your job in these first three levels is to bank chip damage with Q, threaten the double Electro-Harpoon when she overextends, and never let her bait a full commit while your Heat sits at 0 — an Overheat silence here is a free trade for her. Above all, do not dump the cone into a braced Repudiation: the slam that follows scales on exactly what it blocked.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are where this lane flips. Ambessa's W becomes a reliable two-part combo: the first dash to close distance, the second to reposition after your Scrap Shield is spent. She can cycle this faster than your Q heat management allows you to consistently stay in the Danger Zone, and if she catches you at 100 Heat the Overheat silence is an open invitation for a full damage rotation with no defensive tool available. At Level 6 you get a partial answer — The Equalizer dropped across her dash path pins her in your Flamespitter cone and kills her mobility advantage for the duration, so look for that counterplay on every attempted all-in rather than trying to 1v1 her cleanly.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are where this lane flips. Lacerate closes on a 13-second cooldown and Drakehound's Step adds a free dash off every cast, so she cycles in and out faster than your Heat lets you hold the Danger Zone, and at 100 Heat the Overheat silence is an open invitation. Repudiation is the cooldown that decides trades: it is 18 seconds at rank 1, and because the brace turns your sustained cone into a bigger slam, you trade in the window after she spends it and never into it. At 6 The Equalizer laid across her step-out pins her in the cone rather than blocking her, and her Public Execution blinks to the farthest enemy champion in her chosen line — keep a body behind you so that target is not you.

notes: Two things I deliberately did NOT write. First, the kit file puts a 'heal' flag on Public Execution and _missing-interactions.json therefore recommends a Grievous Wounds line for this matchup, but Riot's own Public Execution description contains no healing — blink, suppress, slam, stun, nothing else. Per the rule that the description overrules a misfiring derived flag, I left the anti-heal claims in breakdown.late and the Itemization row untouched rather than either asserting or deleting them; they need a human check. Second, Public Execution suppresses, and whether QSS or Cleanse answers it is exactly the kind of thing the kit file marks unknown, so I said nothing about it. Also unfixable within the length band: full phases[].side still reads Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Rumble against a chart of Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Ambessa/Ambessa/Ambessa/Ambessa. 'Skill' to 'Ambessa' and 'Rumble' to 'Ambessa' are both well outside plus-or-minus 10 percent, so every one of those needs a manual edit. That mismatch is the largest remaining defect in this matchup.
